blocks.h2: What a Red Tag From Nicor Means
blocks.body: If Nicor Gas finds a hazard, it may shut off gas to an appliance or the whole house and leave a red tag. That tag means the problem has to be fixed before service comes back. Call us with what the tag says. We'll find the leak or code issue, repair it, pressure-test the piping and give you what you need to have Nicor come back and restore service.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Questions From Hanover Park Homeowners

items.q: What should I do if I smell gas?
items.preview: Leave and call Nicor Gas or 911.
items.answer: Leave without touching switches. Call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside, then call us.

items.q: Who is responsible for gas piping?
items.preview: Nicor up to the meter. You after it.
items.answer: Nicor Gas handles everything up to and including the meter. Piping after the meter belongs to the homeowner.

items.q: Should I replace old appliance connectors?
items.answer: If they're old uncoated brass, yes. Modern coated connectors are safer.

items.q: How long until service is restored?
items.answer: Once we repair and test the line, Nicor Gas can restore service.

items.q: Can you work on gas lines on the weekend?
items.answer: Yes. Call any time and we'll schedule the repair as soon as we can.

items.q: How much does gas line repair cost in Hanover Park?
items.preview: It depends on the leak. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the leak is and how much pipe needs work. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
